sources.entry: Aegisub - Open-source subtitle editor with timing and styling tools. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Aegisub/Aegisub/) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Aegisub is an open-source subtitle editor, and this repository holds its source code with instructions for building it on Windows and OS X.
summary.what_it_does: The README is mainly a build guide rather than a feature list. It points to a homepage for binaries and general information, and to a bug tracker and forums/IRC for support. The Windows section lists Visual Studio 2015, the June 2010 DirectX SDK and Yasm as prerequisites, and describes cloning the repository with submodules and building a solution. The OS X section covers installing dependencies through Homebrew, building the bundled wxWidgets in vendor/wxWidgets, and running autoreconf, configure and make osx-bundle. It also explains how to update the bundled Moonscript Lua file for the automation scripts. The project is licensed under GPL-compatible BSD-style licenses, and the official Windows and OS X builds are GPLv2 because they include fftw3.
use_cases: Writing or running Lua/Moonscript automation scripts for subtitles
Compiling a subtitle editor on Windows or macOS
how_to_run: Windows: clone recursively with `git clone --recursive git@github.com:Aegisub/Aegisub.git`
Windows: open Aegisub.sln in Visual Studio 2015, build the BuildTasks project, then build the whole solution
OS X: install dependencies with the Homebrew commands listed in the README
OS X: build wxWidgets from vendor/wxWidgets using the configure flags given in the README
OS X: run `autoreconf && ./configure --with-wxdir=/path/to/Aegisub/vendor/wxWidgets && make && make osx-bundle`
notable: Cross-platform build instructions for Windows and OS X, with dependencies stored in the repo or as submodules
Bundled wxWidgets is built with a long, trimmed list of configure flags
Includes a documented procedure for updating the bundled Moonscript file used by automation scripts
Official Windows and OS X builds are GPLv2 because they include fftw3
caveats: Windows build needs the June 2010 DirectX SDK and Visual Studio 2015; the README says the full repository with submodules takes a long time and about 2.5 GB of disk space
OS X build instructions mention older Xcode versions (Xcode 5 or later tested recently), and some Homebrew steps use --HEAD or --devel builds
A full Windows setup needs extra files copied from an installed copy of Aegisub, such as Avisynth and VSFilter
summary.license: GPL-compatible BSD-style licenses (official Windows and OS X builds are GPLv2)
